title: Span Context Rail + Quick Actions — UX runbook (sketches & grooming)
body:
Purpose and context:
This doc captures a focused exploration of a right-side 'Span Context Rail' and inline quick-actions for the trace viewer. It's a working UX runbook for grooming, lightweight wireframe notes, and acceptance criteria that the eng and design teams can iterate on. Goal is to reduce context-switching when investigating a trace, make common remediation actions one click, and keep the waterfall the primary timeline canvas.

Audience:
- Product and design (console + rollouts)
- Serving/runtime and SRE (for data shape and instrumentation)
- Solutions eng / SEs (feedback on workflows)

High-level problem statements:
1) Investigators frequently need span context (request headers, backtrace, sampled logs) while keeping the waterfall visible. Current modal-based details break flow.
2) Common actions (retry, copy payload, open service logs, mark issue) are buried in menus or external tools. These should be discoverable and low-latency.
3) Filters and span grouping are powerful but the interplay between timeline zoom, selected span, and active filters is confusing. We need clear affordances.

Design principles:
- Keep the waterfall timeline as the persistent primary canvas; rail is contextual and dismissible.
- Expose only the 3–5 most-used quick actions by default; hide advanced actions behind an overflow.
- Make keyboard-first interaction possible (power users) while remaining discoverable for new users.
- Degrade gracefully on small screens (rail slides over, not permanently pinned).

Proposed layout (wireframe notes):
- Left/main: Waterfall canvas with spans; timeline ruler and zoom handles remain pinned top.
- Right rail (collapsible): header shows span summary line (service • operation • duration) + micro-status (error/warn/info).
  - Below header: tabs (Details | Logs | Related Traces | Timeline Context).
  - Details tab: key-value list (start, end, duration, host, container, sampling flag, trace_id, span_id). Values should be copyable inline with a small copy icon.
  - Logs tab: last 10 captured logs for that span; each log row has timestamp + message + link to full log in Logs product.
  - Related Traces: suggestions based on same trace_id or same error signature.
  - Timeline Context: shows mini-waterfall focused on sibling/parent spans with toggles to overlay on main canvas.
- Quick actions bar (sticky under header): 4 primary icons with labels on hover: Retry (replay request), Open Service Logs, Copy Payload, Create Incident. Overflow menu for: Export span JSON, Attach to ticket, Annotate span.
- Inline span hover preview: small tooltip that shows first 140 chars of span tags and top-level error message; quarter-second delay on hover to avoid flicker.

Interaction flows and notes:
- Click span => open rail and highlight the span in the main canvas. Rail should animate from right (150ms) with reduced-motion option.
- Esc or click outside => collapse rail. Ctrl/Cmd+Enter when the rail is focused triggers the primary action (Retry).
- Multi-select spans (shift+click or click+drag) => rail switches to 'Group' mode showing aggregated metrics (sum/min/max durations, error counts) and enables bulk quick-actions (bulk export, bulk annotate).
- When filters are changed (e.g., service=auth, status=error), the rail shows a small badge: "filters applied" with a link to reconcile (open a small diff UI showing span visibility changes).
- Zoom sync: if user scrubs time range in the timeline, the rail's Timeline Context updates to reflect new neighbors. Should debounce to avoid jitter (300ms).

Accessibility considerations:
- Ensure rail is accessible with keyboard nav: tab order from timeline -> focused span -> rail header -> quick actions -> tabs -> controls.
- All icons have accessible names and ARIA labels for tooltips.
- Color choices must maintain 4.5:1 contrast for status chips.
- Reduced motion preference collapses entrance animations.

Telemetry and performance constraints (engineering needs):
- Rail data should try to load lazily: header + quick-actions first (single small call), then tabs load on demand. If any tab request is >200ms, show a skeleton placeholder.
- Bulk select should not request per-span details for hundreds of spans; instead request an aggregated summary endpoint. Ticket: JIRA-INF-2145.
- Hover preview should use cached span metadata (from initial trace payload) when possible to avoid extra calls.

Backlog grooming (priority and acceptance criteria):
1) Span Context Rail MVP (P0)
   - AC: click span opens rail showing header, details tab, and quick actions; copy icons for trace/span ids work; Retry action triggers existing replay flow.
   - Linked: JIRA-INF-2145, PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/482
2) Logs in rail (P1)
   - AC: last 10 logs render, link to Logs product opens correct filtered view; fold if none.
3) Group mode + bulk actions (P1)
   - AC: selecting >1 span swaps rail to group view with aggregated metrics; bulk export triggers download of ndjson.
4) Inline hover previews + keyboard shortcuts (P2)
   - AC: hover preview shows tags; keyboard shortcuts documented in help overlay.

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Data retention and payload size: how large can we reasonably show in-rail before we need truncation? (Eng input required)
- Which quick-action should be primary by default? Current leaning: Retry for dev-oriented workflows, Create Incident primary for teams using product heavily in Ops. Consider user toggle.
- Should the rail be pinnable by users (persist across traces)? We should prototype both pinned and ephemeral modes.

Sketch checklist for design handoff:
- [ ] Header microcopy and truncation rules
- [ ] Quick action icons, hover labels, and confirmation flows for destructive actions
- [ ] Tab designs with skeleton states and empty states copy
- [ ] Keyboard shortcut guide modal content and discoverability anchor
- [ ] Accessibility QA checklist + color token mapping

Sample microcopy drafts:
- Header small line: "auth-service · POST /login · 89 ms · ERROR"
- Empty logs state: "No logs captured for this span. Try expanding the trace window or enable span-level logging."
- Hover preview truncated message: "db connection timeout after 120s — see service logs for full backtrace"

Next steps & owners:
- Design: produce two low-fidelity mock variants (rail pinned vs modal-like overlay) — owner: Marta Lopez — due: 2026-01-29.
- Engineering: validate trace payload includes required fields for lazy-loading and aggregated summary — owner: Ben Chu — due: 2026-02-05.
- SRE/observability: confirm log linking patterns and permissions needed — owner: Evan Park — due: 2026-02-12.

Notes to reviewers:
- This is intentionally lightweight; think of it as a runbook + grooming artifact rather than a polished spec. Attach comments inline to this doc and link relevant issues.

Changelog:
- 2026-01-15 Aisha: initial draft
- 2026-02-02 Ben: added telemetry constraints and debounce guidance
- 2026-03-05 Marta: updated acceptance criteria and added sample microcopy
